summary: Elderly woman with known recurrent paroxysmal SVT (previously declined ablation/PPM) presents with palpitations, lightheadedness and a mechanical fall. EMS and ED documented SVT to 150-160s with transient hypotension, converted with adenosine and IV verapamil, with home verapamil uptitrated to 120 mg q8h and resulting asymptomatic Wenckebach. Work-up of the fall showed a nondisplaced comminuted right superior pubic ramus fracture (conservative management, WBAT) and a CT head with no acute intracranial injury; troponin rose 0.02→0.09 with normal CK-MB, interpreted as demand ischemia. Background of CAD, HTN, HLD, depression, presumed untreated urothelial carcinoma, DNR/DNI with transition to home hospice.
most_likely: Recurrent paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (AVNRT) with hemodynamic compromise

supporting_evidence: SVT to 150s found by EMS, cardioverted with adenosine
Recurred in ED; treated with 2x adenosine and IV verapamil
Prior admission principal ICD I471 supraventricular tachycardia
Verapamil increased to 120 mg q8h with good rate control
opposing_evidence: Asymptomatic and in NSR by discharge
differential.reasoning: The presenting arrhythmia is documented, treated and drives the entire admission and medication change; a coder would list this as principal disease.

differential.diagnosis: Closed nondisplaced fracture of right superior pubic ramus from fall
supporting_evidence: Hip X-ray: nondisplaced comminuted right superior pubic ramus fracture
Right hip pain with hip flexion and cross-leg test
Orthopedics recommended conservative management, WBAT, oxycodone
opposing_evidence: Hip non-tender to palpation, no ecchymoses on exam
differential.reasoning: Objectively imaged acute fracture treated during this stay; a strong secondary/co-principal diagnosis with clear resource use.

differential.diagnosis: Type 2 myocardial injury (demand ischemia) due to tachycardia
supporting_evidence: Troponin T rose 0.02 → 0.09 with CK-MB 2 (normal)
Note states 'most likely demand in setting of tachycardia'
ECG unchanged from prior baseline ST changes
opposing_evidence: No chest pain; no new ECG changes; further work-up deferred for goals of care
differential.reasoning: Documented troponin elevation attributed to demand ischemia; codable as NSTEMI/demand ischemia (prior stay coded I214 similarly) but clinically secondary.

differential.diagnosis: Syncope/near-syncope with mechanical fall secondary to arrhythmia
supporting_evidence: Fell when lightheaded, caught fall with arm, no head strike
CT head ordered for post-fall headache — no acute abnormality
Note: falls due to lightheadedness, most likely related to SVT
opposing_evidence: Symptom/mechanism rather than a disease entity
differential.reasoning: Well documented and drives imaging work-up, but is the mechanism of injury rather than a principal disease.

differential.diagnosis: Second degree atrioventricular block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach), drug-related
supporting_evidence: Episodes of Wenckebach on higher dose verapamil during stay
Prior admission coded I441 second degree AV block
Prior Holter showed Wenckebach on nodal blockade
opposing_evidence: Asymptomatic; no intervention required; patient declined PPM
differential.reasoning: Real documented conduction finding attributable to uptitrated verapamil, appropriate as a secondary/complication code.

differential.diagnosis: Presumed urothelial (bladder) carcinoma, untreated, with sterile pyuria
supporting_evidence: Note: likely undiagnosed uroepithelial carcinoma, declined work-up
UA with WBC 45/hpf, RBC 15/hpf; culture mixed flora contaminant
Prior ICD C679 malignant neoplasm of bladder
opposing_evidence: No tissue diagnosis; no imaging of urinary tract this stay
differential.reasoning: Explicitly invoked to explain pyuria and drives hospice transition, though unconfirmed histologically.

differential.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease with hypertension and hyperlipidemia
supporting_evidence: PMH CAD s/p possible MI, HTN, HLD; prior ICD I2510, I10, E785
Continued aspirin 81 mg and rosuvastatin 10 mg during stay
opposing_evidence: No angina; no ischemic work-up this admission; BPs soft (97/61)
differential.reasoning: Chronic comorbidities managed medically this stay; relevant secondary codes but do not explain the acute presentation.

supporting_evidence: Pyuria on UA (WBC 45/hpf); admission WBC 12.2 with neutrophilia
opposing_evidence: Urine culture mixed flora/contaminant, no dysuria, afebrile, WBC normalized to 6.8
differential.reasoning: Considered as an SVT trigger but effectively excluded by culture, absence of symptoms and untreated resolution of leukocytosis.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Acute intracranial hemorrhage / traumatic brain injury after fall
rule_outs.why: CT head showed no acute intracranial abnormality, no fracture; only chronic infarcts
Troponin peak only 0.09 with normal CK-MB, no chest pain, ECG unchanged from baseline

rule_outs.diagnosis: Pneumonia or acute decompensated heart failure
rule_outs.why: CXR showed only low volumes, mild vascular congestion and atelectasis; afebrile, lungs clear

rule_outs.diagnosis: Hip prosthesis loosening or periprosthetic fracture
rule_outs.why: X-ray shows anatomically aligned right hip prosthesis, no lucency, osteolysis or dislocation

uncertain_areas: Whether coders treat SVT or the pubic ramus fracture as the principal diagnosis for this stay
Whether troponin rise was documented as NSTEMI (type 2) versus non-ischemic myocardial injury
Whether verapamil-induced Wenckebach was formally documented as an adverse drug effect
Whether the hospice/palliative-care transition and DNR status were formally coded
Whether pyuria was labeled UTI versus attributed solely to presumed urothelial carcinoma
